items.description:
Artificial intelligence requires safeguards that go beyond self-regulation, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates said in an interview that aired on Sunday, calling for legislation to be passed in Congress.

items.description:
ISLAMABAD: The number of unfrozen lakes in Pakistan grew from 40 to 105 in less than two months, according to satellite imagery assessed by the national space agency of Pakistan between July and August.
Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) said in a press release that the latest assessment was based on temporal satellite imagery, with the the latest image acquired on Aug 5. items.description:

items.description:

items.title: Swiss vote on what it means to be neutral
items.description:
The Swiss voted on Sunday on a much-debated proposal to tighten their country’s cherished neutrality, with polls indicating most would reject the initiative championed by the hard-right and dubbed “pro-Russian” by opponents.
Polling stations opened on Sunday morning for in-person voting on those and other topics as part of Switzerland’s direct democracy system, although most people vote in advance by post.
The Swiss widely embrace their neutrality, but an initiative to enshrine a strict definition into the constitution has exposed deep disagreement over what that neutrality entails.

items.title: Gunmen kill 27 in 2 separate shootings in South Africa
items.description:
Gunmen killed at least 27 people in two mass shootings in South Africa’s two main cities, police said on Sunday, in the latest violence to hit the crime-weary country.
Eight gunmen armed with assault rifles stormed a bar west of Johannesburg at around 1930 GMT (12:30am) on Saturday, killing 17 people and wounding 15 others.
The victims included 13 males and four females.
The suspects opened fire on customers drinking outside and then moved inside to continue shooting, police said.

items.title: Nepal's hydropower ambitions face climate reality check
items.description:
Nepal’s hydropower boom has long been touted as a cornerstone of economic growth and renewable energy, but the devastating flood in August exposed its vulnerability.
The disaster triggered by a glacial mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border killed more than 1,400 people and left thousands missing — while knocking 410 megawatts (MW), or about 10 per cent of the generation capacity, out of Nepal’s power system.

items.description:

“Whether this or that person comes to power, or this party or another —  our people have suffered at the hands of all Israeli parties,”  Khalil al-Hayya told the Qatari station Al-Araby.
